title: Boss Talk with Ben Horowitz
summary: I'm DOS, and this episode is Boss Talk, with A16Z co-founder Ben Horowitz and Databricks CEO, Olly Goadzee, all about leadership and management. Their conversation originally took place on social audio app Clubhouse, where they host a live chat every Tuesday at 5 p.m. You can find more of their and other conversations on our separate feed, A16C live.

positions.commentary: Amazon's culture ensures it will never make products as beautiful as Apple's, while Apple's culture ensures it will never make products as cheap as Amazon's.
Apple's strategy involves building premium, beautiful products that give users status and are not cheap, unlike Amazon.

thesis: This episode contrasts the cultural and strategic identities of Amazon and Apple, arguing that Amazon's 'Day 1' culture supports a low-cost strategy while Apple's culture is dedicated to building premium, beautiful products that confer status. The discussion posits that these opposing cultural principles make it impossible for either company to successfully adopt the other's pricing or product aesthetic strategy.

claims.claim: Amazon is cited as an example of a company with a specific cultural principle ('Day 1') that supports its low-cost strategy, contrasting it with Apple's premium strategy.
claims.quote: is look at Amazon. Amazon has a cultural principle called for Galilee. And that means, you know, everybody's going to, nobody's going to splurge in that company ever. And they're going to be very careful with how to spend their money. And that ensures that fits their whole strategy of going to be the low-cost option.

claims.quote: And they're not cheap. And they're not cheap. And, you know, they'll never make a product as cheap as Amazon. And Amazon will never make a product as beautiful.

claims.quote: And you know who totally doesn't have that cultural value, Apple? Yeah. because they've got a $5 billion like campus. And they've got doorknobs that probably cost more than anything at Amazon.
